subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers adopt the open conflicting fork PR for this issue, request a clean replacement, or leave the current gateway/TUI title behavior unchanged?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but an open closing-syntax PR already owns the attempted fix and is currently conflicting, so automation should not queue a second fix until maintainers choose the branch path.

options.title: Adopt or replace the linked fix
options.body: Review the open fork PR and either make it clean or authorize a narrow replacement PR that preserves the same title precedence and metadata stripping behavior.

options.title: Defer to broader title work
options.body: Keep this bug open until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/81781 is designed, accepting that the metadata-title leak remains in the meantime.

options.title: Close as acceptable behavior
options.body: Close only if maintainers intentionally accept raw gateway transcript metadata as a title fallback, which the current evidence does not support.

recommendation.title: Adopt or replace the linked fix
recommendation.body: Review the open fork PR and either make it clean or authorize a narrow replacement PR that preserves the same title precedence and metadata stripping behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway/session-list refactors and current-main ownership signals make this the best available routing candidate for the branch-path decision.
